title: Dividing out a factor with x in it
problem: An AI tutor was asked for all real solutions of \((x^2 + 1)(x - 3) = 2(x^2 + 1)\). Tap a slip if you spot one, or call it clean.
steps: For every real number \(x\), \(x^2 \ge 0\), so \(x^2 + 1 \ge 1 > 0\) is never zero.
Divide both sides by \(x^2 + 1\) to get \(x - 3 = 2\).
Check in the original: \((5^2 + 1)(5 - 3) = 26 \cdot 2 = 52\) and \(2(5^2 + 1) = 52\), so \(x = 5\) is the only real solution.

meta.blurb: It divided both sides by an expression containing \(x\) — did it quietly drop a root?

explanation: Dividing by \(x^2 + 1\) looks like a lost-root trap, except \(x^2 + 1 \ge 1\) can never hit zero for any real \(x\).
